title: Mercenary captain
note: Officer frames 208x188 (troops are 156x174). The figure is drawn at the troops' pixel density (1 art px = 2x2 native, same outline and shading) but 1.08x taller, so an officer stands a head above his men when both are shown at one scale.

anchor.desc: feet on native row 182 (6 px above the frame bottom, as the troops); body centred at frameWidth/2. Same origin rule as the troops: origin = (x/frameWidth, (y+1)/frameHeight).

measured.inGame: BattleScene.singleSprite shows it at setScale(0.5): 281 px frame, ~250 px body on screen

scaleReference.match: same framing as the elite (body 0.92 of frame height vs the elite 0.883-0.916). Displayed at 1.5x (282 px frame) an officer is the same on-screen size as the elite at 0.5x, and every art pixel becomes an exact 3x3 block (no blur).

description: Mercenary captain. Slashed doublet (cloth1 over cloth3 lining) and puffed sleeves, steel breastplate and tassets with gilt trim, cocked oxblood bonnet with red and blue ostrich plumes, oxblood half-cloak, goatee, two-handed greatsword.

palette.swapHint: Faction swap = cloth1 (main garment) + paint (faction accent) ONLY. accent2 is a second, fixed accent (oxblood) that never swaps, so one faction colour cannot swallow the figure. cloth2 / cloth3 = secondary cloth and patches, gilt = brass trim, fur = collar. "Faded" is done inside the cloth1 ramp (lighter, noisier steps), never with extra colours. Checked in code: no colour outside these ramps.

factionSwap.rule: faction versions replace the cloth1 and paint ramps colour-for-colour (same length); every other ramp, including accent2, keeps its colours. 8-bit walkers: cloth1 = O/C, paint = E/R/a, accent2 = r (its own key).

parts.accent2: bonnet (was cloth1) + half-cloak (was paint): the League swap no longer turns bonnet, doublet, cape and plume all gold (shot 52b/52c)

kitLayers.source: src/kits.py (KITS["captain"]); layer functions in src/captains.py, registered into the figure.py registries (BODIES / ARMOUR / HAIRS / HELMETS / SHIELDS / PAULDRONS / FACE_EXTRA / POLE / CAPES).

nesMapping.paletteSource: reference/nes-palette.js (exact colours only; alpha 0 or 255; no anti-aliasing; dithering allowed)

skin.why: face T, shade a (standard NES skin pair); R only for the deepest crease. Not C: C is the jack/wood highlight.

hair.why: dark brown D; no highlight step, so hair and beard stay one flat mass like the warden walker hood.

cloth1.why: muted tan has no true NES match. O (ochre) is the closest perceptually, with C for quilting/highlight lines and D for shadow. Not T (reads as skin) and not Y/y (League gold).

cloth2.why: olive-grey hose/sleeves read as neutral grey S. NES has no desaturated olive; G/g are Covenant green. The 16-bit ramp was nudged greyer so the two tiers agree.

leather.why: boots, belt, gloves = D; the brightest leather step lifts to O only if a highlight is needed.

metal.why: grey steps S/s/w. The kettle hat is drawn one step up (s body, S shade, w glint) so it stays the brightest thing on the walker, as in the 16-bit art.

paint.why: shield face E (orange-red), rim/shade R, glint a. The 16-bit paint ramp was changed from ochre to red-orange because ochre mapped to O, the same colour as the jack.

cloth3.why: woad-blue hoods/caps: body n, highlight i. The 16-bit ramp was changed from a pale slate grey-blue (no NES match; its nearest colour, grey S, would make the hood read as the warden walker) to a clearer woad blue so both tiers agree.

gilt.why: brass/gilt trim (P2 officers) = O with a C glint, D shade. Its Lab-nearest light steps are y/Y, but those are kept free for the League gold, so gilt stays O/C (1-2 px on a walker, reads as brass next to the S steel).

accent2.why: oxblood accent (P2 officers: chief buckler face, sergeant sash, captain bonnet + cape) = r (deep red) with K shade. Lab-nearest is R, but R is the paint ramp's shade: r keeps accent2 on its own NES key, so an 8-bit faction swap that maps the paint keys (E/R/a) or the cloth1 keys (O/C) never touches it. accent2 is NOT faction-swapped (16-bit or 8-bit).

outline.why: both outline rings become black K, as on the warden walker in 16-road-highland-moor.png. m (#940084) is the nearest hue to the magenta outer ring, but the road ground dither uses it, so an m outline would dissolve into the ground.

nesMapping.avoid: In this neutral scheme, keep G/g/l (Covenant green), P/p/L (Nightglass violet) and Y/y (League gold) free for faction versions. Faction swaps change cloth1 and paint only; accent2 (NES r) and every other ramp stay fixed.
nesMapping.pickRule: labNearest is the raw nearest colour. Where the pick differs, it was chosen so the material still reads as the same material, e.g. skin mid-tones go a/T rather than D (brown dirt), and the jack mid-tone goes O rather than D/S (so it reads as tan cloth, not hair or steel).
nesMapping.dENote: dE is a Lab distance (nes.py) from the 16-bit colour to the picked NES colour; big values mean the NES palette has no close match.

nesCarryOver.walkerCanvas: 16x22 per frame, 4 frames (64x22 strip: A contact, B passing, C contact, D passing), facing right, feet on row 21, body centre x=8; same LEGS/BOB cycle as the P1 walkers so officers march in step with their troops
mustCarryOver: flat cocked oxblood bonnet (r, accent2) with a big red-orange ostrich plume (E/a, paint = faction accent) and a blue plume (n) swept back
oxblood cape (r, K edge; accent2, fixed in faction swaps) hanging off the back shoulder - the only caped unit
steel breastplate (s, w glint) with gilt (O/C) edge, S tassets
doublet + puffed sleeves: O with n slashes (cloth1 = the faction colour, cloth3 lining)
two-handed greatsword carried upright, blade s/w, wide S cross-guard with O (gilt) ends, D grip
nesCarryOver.mustNotHappen: bonnet and cape must stay on accent2 (r): if they go back onto cloth1/paint a faction swap turns the whole captain one colour (shot 52b/52c).

notes.idle: greatsword resting on the near shoulder, both hands on the grip.
notes.attack: greatsword cut from the shoulder: windup lifts the blade back over the head, attack sweeps it forward and down (foreshortened).
notes.hit: frame 0 is a built-in brightness flash that stays inside the ramps (palette-swap safe).
notes.rout: 4 frames: frame 0 = turning away, frames 1-3 = running away seen from behind (screen-right). Play once, then loop frames 1-3 while he leaves. There is no back sheet (front view only, as briefed).
notes.death: 6 frames: stagger, knees buckle, slump, topple back, lying (2). The weapon drops to the ground on frame 2. The lowest body pixel of every death frame sits on the anchor (ground) row 182.
notes.frameMargin: every frame keeps >= 6 native px clear on the left, right and top (checked in code, src/build.py MARGIN). The bottom is the anchor: feet on row 182, 5 px above the frame edge, as briefed.
notes.recover: 2 frames, blade returns low and round then up onto the shoulder: figure width attack 124/140/126 -> recover 112/110 -> idle 108 px (was 138 -> 88 -> 108, which popped).

revisions: 2026-09-30: death-row grounding fix: the lowest body pixel of every death frame now sits on row 182 (was measured from the in-hand weapon, so the body floated); death row only, every other row pixel-identical

2026-09-30 rev b (shots 49-52c): recover row re-posed (width 138 -> 88 px pop is now 112 -> 110 -> idle 108); 6 px margin: death frame 2 shifted 2 px left (reached x203), attack-0 blade tipped 6 deg lower, plumes swept down in the run frames; bonnet (cloth1) and cape (paint) moved to accent2 (oxblood, fixed in faction swaps), so the faction colour is the doublet, sleeves and big plume. Re-posed rows: attack, recover, death (frame 2 shift only), rout. idle, windup, hit: same pixels, only bonnet + cape recoloured.
